sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: The areca or betel-nut palm is a slender tropical tree native to the Philippines and widely cultivated across South and Southeast Asia and the Pacific. It can exceed 15 m; the crown carries long pinnate leaves. Its orange-red fibrous fruit is about 5 cm long and contains the seed called areca nut.

sections.title: Food and toxicity
sections.text: The seed is chewed in some cultural traditions, often with betel leaf (Piper betle), lime and sometimes tobacco. Areca nut itself is carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 1); betel leaf and the palm's seed are different plants and parts. The plate's palm and fruit correspond to the species.
